prize_parts.citation: For the experimental discovery of the Higgs boson, through the conception, construction and leadership of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the Large Hadron Collider

statement.case_for: The 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson by two independent general-purpose detectors completed the Standard Model and verified the mechanism recognised theoretically in 2013, which left the experimental discovery itself without a prize. It is original as a feat of detector design and analysis, and the ensuing mass, spin-parity and coupling measurements have made its meaning stable for over a decade. Four of eight members ranked it first and seven ranked it, so the support comes from members with very different fields. The case rests on science, not on the vote tally: no other shortlisted entry combines a decisive, unambiguous discovery with this level of independent confirmation. The attribution problem is real but is a reason to choose the names carefully, not a reason to defer a result that is already overdue.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is attribution. Two collaborations of thousands made the discovery, the statutes cap the prize at three, and the credited list contains four leaders, so any trio omits someone with a serious claim and is partly a prize for leadership rather than for a single identifiable invention. A related objection is policy: the Academy may be reluctant to honour collaboration spokespersons, and it may judge that the 2013 theory prize already settled the topic. If the committee finds no defensible trio, a clean theory-plus-experiment or invention-plus-realisation entry such as the optical lattice clock (B013) is the safer choice, and I regard that as a serious alternative, not a token one.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B001 first and proposes Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee, noting that Della Negra is a strong alternative and that the configuration is open to dispute.
responses.response: We agree on the science and on Gianotti and Jenni; our only difference is Virdee versus Della Negra as the CMS name. I do not think the supplied evidence settles that choice, and I would not treat my own pick as uniquely correct. I keep Della Negra because I weigh the founding conception of CMS most heavily, but I would accept Virdee if the committee finds a stronger documented case for his role in the CMS design and delivery. The cleaner point we share is the 2+1 balance between ATLAS and CMS.

responses.point: Pearce ranks B001 first but proposes two CMS-side names (Gianotti with Della Negra and Virdee), and ranks IceCube (B059) second as an instrument-driven opening of a new observational window.
responses.response: I disagree with a configuration that leaves out Jenni. That would give CMS two seats and ATLAS one, and Jenni is the founding ATLAS spokesperson, so the balance looks harder to defend than 2+1 either way. I accept your point that this is a judgement about leadership and not a verified accounting. On IceCube, I agree it is a real new window, but the source identification is still statistically modest and I rank it well below the Higgs on maturity; I would not put it in the preferred configuration.

responses.point: Eriksson ranks dynamical mean-field theory (B043) first as a conceptually clean, widely used framework for correlated electrons, and ranks B001 only fifth because choosing three of four names is arbitrary.
responses.response: I take the attribution worry seriously and share it, but I do not agree that it should move B001 down to fifth. The difficulty is in who is named, not in whether the discovery is prize-worthy. On DMFT, I accept it is conceptually elegant and influential. It is a theoretical method whose success varies by material, and its credit, including Metzner who is not in the credited names, is less settled than you suggest. I would not put it ahead of a confirmed discovery, but I see no need to force agreement here and note that only you ranked it first.

responses.point: Lindroth ranks the optical lattice clock (B013) first and proposes only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero for twisted bilayer graphene (B046), leaving out Bistritzer.
responses.response: I fully agree that B013 is a strong candidate and it is my own second choice, with a clean Katori and Ye pairing. I would not rank it above the Higgs, because the redefinition of the second is still pending and the 2005 comb prize partly overlaps. On B046, I think dropping Bistritzer is hard to justify: the continuum-model prediction is a joint paper, and splitting it would be an arbitrary choice that weakens the theory side of the pairing. If the committee goes to B046 I would keep all three credited names, though I still consider it somewhat early.

responses.point: Kroll ranks B013 first and circuit QED (B054) second, and discloses a possible perceived tie to John Hall's laboratory in relation to Ye.
responses.response: Your disclosure is useful and I do not think it undermines the clock case, which stands on independent confirmation in several laboratories. I will not argue for B054 on the merits, because of my own connections (see conflict note), so I leave the circuit QED case to colleagues without a link. I would note that the 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, and I think the committee should weigh the proximity in time and subject even if the discovery is distinct.

uncertainties: Which of the four credited names (Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni, Virdee) should be left out, and whether the committee will accept a leadership-based trio for two collaborations of thousands.
Whether the 2013 theory prize makes the Academy less willing to recognise the experimental discovery now.
My recollection of individual roles (spokesperson terms, detector conception) comes from general knowledge and is not verified from the supplied evidence.
Whether the committee prefers B013 as a cleaner configuration if it cannot agree on the Higgs names.
statement.conflict_note: I am a professor at Chalmers and director of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology, and my own work is in superconducting circuits and circuit QED. B054 (Blais, Wallraff, Schoelkopf) is in my subject area and close to the work of my Chalmers colleagues and WACQT, so I would recuse myself from deciding that entry. The 2025 laureates also visited Chalmers. I have no documented personal or institutional connection to the preferred B001 configuration (Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni) or to the alternatives B013 and B046 in the provided profile.
